title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The previous page is a cover sheet: 'Groupoïde fondamental d'une courbe tame (préliminaires à l'action de Galois), 14 pages'. This page opens that bundle. It works out combinatorial presentations of the fundamental groupoid of X = P^1_C − {0,1,∞} relative to various sets of base points adapted to the real structure.

(1) Main diagram: 6 vertices, 9 arrows, 2 relations.
- At each puncture p ∈ {0,1,∞}, Grothendieck draws a small circle and places two base points on it, where the circle meets the real line P^1(R). In modern terms these are the six tangential base points →01, →0∞, →10, →1∞, →∞0, →∞1.
- Arrows a^p: the three real intervals of P^1(R) − {0,1,∞}. Each a^p is the interval opposite to p: a^∞ = ]0,1[, a^0 joins 1 and ∞, a^1 joins ∞ and 0.
- Arrows λ^p_±: half-loops around p, in the upper half-plane (+) or lower half-plane (−).
- The graph is embedded in the sphere. By Euler, V − E + F = 6 − 9 + F = 2, so F = 5: the three punctured discs plus the two hemispheres (upper and lower half-planes).
- Only the two hemispheres are genuine 2-cells. They give the 2 relations, namely the boundary hexagons. The upper one reads λ^0_+ a^∞ λ^1_+ a^0 λ^∞_+ a^1 = 1, and the lower one is the same with λ_− and the orientation reversed.
- Check: rank = 9 − 6 + 1 − 2 = 2, matching π_1 = F_2.
- Complex conjugation swaps the + and − half-loops, and S_3 permutes everything.

(2) Reduction: 4 vertices, 6 arrows, 1 relation, '3 cas'.
- At two punctures the pair of base points is collapsed to one, and the two half-loops are fused into full loops Λ^∞_+ and Λ^0_+. The interval a^1 is dropped, which merges the two hemispheres into a single cell.
- Two base points and the half-loops λ^1_± are kept at the remaining puncture.
- Rank = 6 − 4 + 1 − 1 = 2. There are 3 cases according to which puncture keeps two base points.

(3) A struck-out attempt, then: 2 vertices (at 0 and 1), 3 arrows (a^∞, Λ^0, Λ'^1), 0 relations.
- The loops based at 0 and 1 satisfy Λ^0_+ = (Λ^0_−)^{-1} and Λ'^1_− = (Λ'^1_+)^{-1}.
- This is a free groupoid of rank 2. There are 3 cases, by choice of the interval.

(4) 1 vertex, 2 arrows, 0 relations.
- The base point is at 0, with generators Λ^0_+ and A^{01}_+, the latter being the loop around 1 transported along a^∞.
- This gives the free group F_2 = ⟨x, y⟩ in its familiar form. There are 3 cases.

Purpose: to get an S_3- and complex-conjugation-compatible presentation of the 'tame' fundamental groupoid. On this presentation Gal(Q̄/Q) is to act by fixing the real arcs up to an element f and raising the half-loops to χ(σ)-type powers. This is exactly the set-up that later yields the GT hexagon relation: f(x,y) x^m f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m = 1 is the image of the upper-hemisphere hexagon.

Dating: show-through of a typed Montpellier seminar announcement of 24.03.80 (the next archive page) suggests the sheet is its verso. That would place this page around or after March 1980, before Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara.
errors: No mathematical errors; the vertex/arrow/relation counts are all consistent with χ(P^1−3 pts) = −1, i.e. π_1 free of rank 2.
Minor notational inconsistency: Λ'^1 (primed) is used in the 2-vertex case, versus λ^1 elsewhere.
In the 1-vertex case the upper/lower choice for A^{01} is indicated only by the subscript +, while the '3 cas' counting is left implicit.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} on six tangential base points (two at each puncture, along the real line), generated by the three real intervals and six half-loops, with two hexagonal relations from the upper and lower half-planes.
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} with the six tangential base points →01, →10, etc.; half-loops; hexagon cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne 1989. Half-loop/hexagon presentation: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara 1990s, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller groupoid with base points and the role of M_{0,4}/M_{0,5}, but not this explicit 6-vertex presentation

ideas.what: Successive reductions of the base-point set (6 → 4 → 2 → 1) while keeping S_3-compatible presentations, each counted as '3 cas'.
ideas.modern_name: Change of base-point sets in free groupoids; equivalence of presentations

ideas.what: Using the real structure P^1(R) ⊂ P^1(C) as a cell decomposition, so that complex conjugation exchanges λ_+ and λ_−.
ideas.modern_name: Real/dessin cell structure of P^1; complex conjugation in GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara; implicit in dessins d'enfants

missed.claim: The page explicitly records the two-hexagon cell structure (real intervals plus half-loops at six tangential base points) as the presentation on which the Galois action is to be studied. This is the topological source of the GT hexagon relation, apparently written c. 1980, a decade before Drinfeld and Ihara.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it documents that Grothendieck had the half-loop/hexagon groupoid with six tangential base points (the heart of the definition of GT) early. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is now textbook (Deligne's tangential base points, Drinfeld–Ihara hexagon). The interest is an early and explicit appearance in Grothendieck's hand, probably c. 1980 given the show-through dating, which precedes the published literature.
transcription_corrections: First diagram: the label on the arrow from 0 to 1 appears as a^∞ with a small subscript (possibly 'a_0^∞'), not plain a^∞.
Second diagram: the labels at 1 are λ^1_+ and λ^1_− (half-loops), while those at 0 and ∞ are capital Λ^0_+ and Λ^∞_+ (full loops).
Struck-out text reads '1 cas'; the drawing includes an arrow from 1 to ∞ and an arc from 0 to 1.
Faint typed text showing through (seminar announcement of 24.03.80, M. Coste, Micali) indicates the sheet is the verso of the next archive page; this is a dating clue, not part of the notes.
